newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss central bank says it has no Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Swiss central bank says it has no Nazi gold.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank, under fire for buying Nazi German bullion during World War Two, said on Friday it no longer held any gold bars from Hitler's Reichsbank.

The Swiss central bank also rejected calls from the World Jewish Congress and a U.S. senator for an immediate Swiss payment to Holocaust survivors as compensation for profiting from war-era business with Nazis and their Jewish victims.

SNB vice-chairman Jean-Pierre Roth said a sweep of the vaults found no bars stamped with the seal of the Reichsbank, the Nazi central bank that sold the SNB 1.2 billion Swiss francs worth of gold between 1939 and 1945.
"Our investigations have shown that we no longer hold any ingots bearing German stamps," Roth said.
Roth said a large part of the German deliveries had been passed on to other countries in the course of routine gold transactions between central banks during or after the war.
"The remainder, together with gold ingots of differing origins, was used for minting coins after the war," he said.
Switzerland's central bank is under fire from critics who say its dealings with the Reichsbank allowed Hitler to launder gold stolen from occupied countries and death camp prisoners into clean cash.

SNB chairman Hans Meyer said at a joint news conference with Roth that it was difficult to understand how the bank's World War Two-era directors believed German assurances that their gold was not stolen from occupied countries.
"We believe they thought too little about the political implications of their actions," Meyer said.
Meyer said the SNB supported a probe by historians and experts being launched by the government into a range of Swiss financial dealings during the war, including the gold purchases.
But Meyer said the historical commission, which is due to start work in early 1997 after final approval was granted by parliament this week, must be given time to reach its findings.
"We believe that conclusions should not be jumped to before the results, that we should not discuss any substantial advanced payments before facts are available," Meyer said.

World Jewish Congress president Edgar Bronfman and U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato called this week for a Swiss gesture to compensate ageing Holocaust survivors rather than make them wait for the Berne commission's results in two or three years.

The SNB Nazi gold purchases are part of a complex of charges levelled at Switzerland by critics like the WJC and D'Amato, who also say Swiss banks profited cynically from Nazi deposits and sat on accounts left ownerless by Jews killed in the Holocaust.

Besides the historical commission, Swiss banks have also launched two parallel probes, including one with world Jewish groups, aimed at uncovering ownerless Holocaust accounts and finding the rightful heirs.
